note: F4: there is no single flame that has burned since antiquity. Each synagogue keeps its own lamp alight, and modern lamps are usually electric.

replace: Orthodox Jews regard the Torah as the direct, verbatim word of G-d dictated to Moses
note: F8: only the Torah is held to have been given word for word to Moses. Nevi'im and Ketuvim are later prophecy and inspired writing.

find: They cover duties to G-d (no other gods, no images, Sabbath observance, honouring the divine name) and duties to other people (honouring parents, prohibitions on murder, adultery, theft, false witness, and coveting).
replace: Jewish tradition divides them five and five. The first five are duties to G-d: G-d’s own declaration “I am the Lord your God”, no other gods or images, not misusing the divine name, keeping Shabbat, and honouring parents. The second five are duties to other people: no murder, no adultery, no theft, no false witness and no coveting.
note: F7: honouring parents is the fifth commandment and belongs on the first tablet in the Jewish division. The old text used the Christian grouping.
